section_1.title: The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'updating belief' through a story. A detective dog named 'Sherlock Bones' hears a rustle in the bushes. He thinks there's a 10% chance it's a cat. If it were a cat, his ears would twitch with 90% certainty. His ears just twitched. Does this mean it's definitely a cat? This sets the stage for prior vs. posterior probability.
section_1.example: Visual: Sherlock Bones with a thought bubble showing a 'Cat' (10%) and 'Wind' (90%). An animation shows his ears twitching as the 'new evidence'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Conditional Probability & The Shrinking Universe
section_2.content: Explain P(A|B) using a Venn Diagram. Emphasize that 'Given B' means our 'Universe' (Sample Space) shrinks from the whole rectangle to just circle B. We are now looking for the area where A and B overlap within that new, smaller circle.
section_2.example: Animation: A large square (Total Probability) fades out, leaving only a glowing circle 'B'. A small slice of 'A' inside 'B' is highlighted to represent P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).

section_3.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
section_3.content: Define Independence. If A and B are independent, knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). This means the 'proportion' of A inside B is the same as A's proportion in the whole universe.
section_3.example: Visual: Two circles (A and B) that don't overlap in a way that suggests dependency. If we zoom into B, the percentage of A remains exactly the same as it was in the original square.

section_4.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
section_4.content: Derive Bayes' Theorem by combining the conditional probability formulas. Show how P(A|B) allows us to reverse the condition to find P(B|A). Focus on the components: Prior P(A), Likelihood P(B|A), and Evidence P(B).
section_4.example: Graphic: A balance scale. On one side is our 'Prior belief' (P(A)). We add 'Evidence' (the Likelihood ratio) to tip the scale toward the 'Posterior' result.

section_5.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
section_5.content: Apply the theorem to a classic false-positive scenario. A 'Quality Control Robot' scans chips. 1% of chips are defective (Prior). The robot is 99% accurate but has a 5% false alarm rate. If the robot beeps, what is the actual chance the chip is broken? This highlights how even 'good' evidence can be misleading if the prior is low.
section_5.example: Tree Diagram: Start with 1,000 chips. Branch into 10 Defective and 990 Healthy. Show the robot's 'Beep' paths. Most beeps actually come from healthy chips (False Positives), surprising the learner.

section_6.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
section_6.content: Briefly explain what happens to Bayes' Theorem if events are independent. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) simply equals P(A). The evidence B becomes 'noise' and doesn't update our belief about A at all.
section_6.example: Visual: A 'Bayes Machine' where the input 'Evidence B' passes through a filter. If B is independent of A, the output (Posterior) is identical to the input (Prior).

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_7.content: Summarize: 1. Bayes' Theorem is a way to update beliefs. 2. Independence means evidence is irrelevant. 3. Always consider the Prior (the base rate) before jumping to conclusions.
section_7.example: Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat' after combining his twitching ears with the base rate of cats in the neighborhood.

section_4.content: Derive Bayes' Theorem by combining the conditional probability formulas. Show how P(A|B) allows us to reverse the condition to find P(B|A). Focus on the components: Prior P(A), Likelihood P(B|A), and Evidence P(B).
section_4.example: Graphic: A balance scale. On one side is our 'Prior belief' (P(A)). We add 'Evidence' (the Likelihood ratio) to tip the scale toward the 'Posterior' result.

section_5.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
section_5.content: Apply the theorem to a classic false-positive scenario. A 'Quality Control Robot' scans chips. 1% of chips are defective (Prior). The robot is 99% accurate but has a 5% false alarm rate. If the robot beeps, what is the actual chance the chip is broken? This highlights how even 'good' evidence can be misleading if the prior is low.
section_5.example: Tree Diagram: Start with 1,000 chips. Branch into 10 Defective and 990 Healthy. Show the robot's 'Beep' paths. Most beeps actually come from healthy chips (False Positives), surprising the learner.

section_6.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
section_6.content: Briefly explain what happens to Bayes' Theorem if events are independent. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) simply equals P(A). The evidence B becomes 'noise' and doesn't update our belief about A at all.
section_6.example: Visual: A 'Bayes Machine' where the input 'Evidence B' passes through a filter. If B is independent of A, the output (Posterior) is identical to the input (Prior).

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_7.content: Summarize: 1. Bayes' Theorem is a way to update beliefs. 2. Independence means evidence is irrelevant. 3. Always consider the Prior (the base rate) before jumping to conclusions.
section_7.example: Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat' after combining his twitching ears with the base rate of cats in the neighborhood.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma
lecture_lines: Meet Sherlock Bones, our probabilistic detective dog.
He hears a rustle in the bushes nearby.
Sherlock believes there's a 10% chance it's a cat.
If it's a cat, his ears twitch 90% often.
His ears just twitched! Is it really a cat?
animations: Fade in Sherlock Bones dog icon.
Display thought bubble: Cat (10%) vs Wind (90%).
Change color of 'Cat (10%)' to #FFFF00 to show Prior.
Animate ears twitching on the dog icon.
Question text 'P(Cat | Twitch)?' fades in at center.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Conditional Probability & The Shrinking Universe
lecture_lines: Conditional probability looks at a specific subset of outcomes.
If event B occurs, our entire universe shrinks.
We only care about A where it overlaps B.
animations: Show Venn Diagram with circles A and B.
Fade out everything except circle B and A \cap B.
Show formula P(A|B) = P(A \cap B) / P(B) next to Venn.

section_3.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
lecture_lines: Independence means event B provides no new information.
Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A.
The proportion of A remains constant across the universe.
animations: Show two circles A and B inside a square.
Highlight circle A, then highlight the portion of A in B.
Show P(A|B) = P(A) to indicate no change in ratio.

section_4.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.
Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.
Multiply by the likelihood of seeing this evidence.
Divide by the total probability of that evidence.
Now you have the updated posterior probability.
animations: Write the full Bayes formula P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).
Highlight P(A) in #FFFF00 and label it 'Prior'.
Highlight P(B|A) in #00FF00 and label it 'Likelihood'.
Highlight P(B) in #00FFFF and label it 'Evidence'.
Highlight P(A|B) in #FF00FF and label it 'Posterior'.

section_5.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
lecture_lines: A robot scans chips for rare defects.
Only 1% of chips are actually defective.
The robot is 99% accurate but has false alarms.
If it beeps, is the chip definitely broken?
Surprisingly, most beeps come from healthy chips!
animations: Start Tree Diagram with 1000 Chips at the top.
Branch to 10 Defective and 990 Healthy nodes.
Extend branches for 'Beep' (9.9 from Def, 49.5 from Healthy).
Circle all 'Beep' nodes in #FF0000.
Show P(Defective | Beep) calculation: 9.9 / (9.9 + 49.5).

section_6.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
lecture_lines: What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?
The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.
Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior.
animations: Show P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B).
Replace P(B|A) with P(B) using a sliding animation.
Strike through P(B) in both parts to reveal P(A).

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem is a tool for updating beliefs.
Always consider the prior base rate first.
Evidence is only useful if it's dependent.
animations: Animate an arrow from 'Prior' to 'Posterior'.
Cross out 'Evidence' for independent events.
Show Sherlock Bones successfully finding the cat.

outline.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
outline.content: Apply the theorem to a classic false-positive scenario. A 'Quality Control Robot' scans chips. 1% of chips are defective (Prior). The robot is 99% accurate but has a 5% false alarm rate. If the robot beeps, what is the actual chance the chip is broken? This highlights how even 'good' evidence can be misleading if the prior is low.

outline.title: The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma

outline.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
outline.content: Define Independence. If A and B are independent, knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). This means the 'proportion' of A inside B is the same as A's proportion in the whole universe.
outline.example: Visual: Two circles (A and B) that don't overlap in a way that suggests dependency. If we zoom into B, the percentage of A remains exactly the same as it was in the original square.

storyboard.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
lecture_lines: Independence means event B provides no new information.
Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A.
The proportion of A remains constant across the universe.
animations: Show two circles A and B inside a square.
Highlight circle A, then highlight the portion of A in B.
Show P(A|B) = P(A) to indicate no change in ratio.

outline.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
outline.content: Derive Bayes' Theorem by combining the conditional probability formulas. Show how P(A|B) allows us to reverse the condition to find P(B|A). Focus on the components: Prior P(A), Likelihood P(B|A), and Evidence P(B).
outline.example: Graphic: A balance scale. On one side is our 'Prior belief' (P(A)). We add 'Evidence' (the Likelihood ratio) to tip the scale toward the 'Posterior' result.

storyboard.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.
Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.
Multiply by the likelihood of seeing this evidence.
Divide by the total probability of that evidence.
Now you have the updated posterior probability.
animations: Write the full Bayes formula P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).
Highlight P(A) in #FFFF00 and label it 'Prior'.
Highlight P(B|A) in #00FF00 and label it 'Likelihood'.
Highlight P(B) in #00FFFF and label it 'Evidence'.
Highlight P(A|B) in #FF00FF and label it 'Posterior'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        color_posterior = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        color_likelihood = "#00FF00" # Green
        color_prior = "#FFFF00"      # Yellow
        color_evidence = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        color_highlight = WHITE

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Independence in Bayes' Context",
            [
                "What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?",
                "The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.",
                "Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)
        # Using MathTex with parts for coloring and animation
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}",
            font_size=42
        )
        # Set colors
        formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        # index 2 is P(B|A)
        formula[2].set_color(color_likelihood)
        # index 4 is P(A)
        formula[4].set_color(color_prior)
        # index 6 is P(B)
        formula[6].set_color(color_evidence)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Replace P(B|A) with P(B)
        # New likelihood term
        new_likelihood = MathTex("P(B)", font_size=42, color=color_evidence)
        new_likelihood.move_to(formula[2].get_center())
        
        # Sliding animation: show the swap
        self.play(
            formula[2].animate.shift(UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * 0.5).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(new_likelihood, shift=DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)

            "Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.",
            "Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.",

section_1.title: The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'updating belief' through a story. A detective dog named 'Sherlock Bones' hears a rustle in the bushes. He thinks there's a 10% chance it's a cat. If it were a cat, his ears would twitch with 90% certainty. His ears just twitched. Does this mean it's definitely a cat? This sets the stage for prior vs. posterior probability.
section_1.example: Visual: Sherlock Bones with a thought bubble showing a 'Cat' (10%) and 'Wind' (90%). An animation shows his ears twitching as the 'new evidence'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Conditional Probability & The Shrinking Universe
section_2.content: Explain P(A|B) using a Venn Diagram. Emphasize that 'Given B' means our 'Universe' (Sample Space) shrinks from the whole rectangle to just circle B. We are now looking for the area where A and B overlap within that new, smaller circle.
section_2.example: Animation: A large square (Total Probability) fades out, leaving only a glowing circle 'B'. A small slice of 'A' inside 'B' is highlighted to represent P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).

section_3.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
section_3.content: Define Independence. If A and B are independent, knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). This means the 'proportion' of A inside B is the same as A's proportion in the whole universe.
section_3.example: Visual: Two circles (A and B) that don't overlap in a way that suggests dependency. If we zoom into B, the percentage of A remains exactly the same as it was in the original square.

section_4.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
section_4.content: Derive Bayes' Theorem by combining the conditional probability formulas. Show how P(A|B) allows us to reverse the condition to find P(B|A). Focus on the components: Prior P(A), Likelihood P(B|A), and Evidence P(B).
section_4.example: Graphic: A balance scale. On one side is our 'Prior belief' (P(A)). We add 'Evidence' (the Likelihood ratio) to tip the scale toward the 'Posterior' result.

section_5.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
section_5.content: Apply the theorem to a classic false-positive scenario. A 'Quality Control Robot' scans chips. 1% of chips are defective (Prior). The robot is 99% accurate but has a 5% false alarm rate. If the robot beeps, what is the actual chance the chip is broken? This highlights how even 'good' evidence can be misleading if the prior is low.
section_5.example: Tree Diagram: Start with 1,000 chips. Branch into 10 Defective and 990 Healthy. Show the robot's 'Beep' paths. Most beeps actually come from healthy chips (False Positives), surprising the learner.

section_6.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
section_6.content: Briefly explain what happens to Bayes' Theorem if events are independent. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) simply equals P(A). The evidence B becomes 'noise' and doesn't update our belief about A at all.
section_6.example: Visual: A 'Bayes Machine' where the input 'Evidence B' passes through a filter. If B is independent of A, the output (Posterior) is identical to the input (Prior).

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_7.content: Summarize: 1. Bayes' Theorem is a way to update beliefs. 2. Independence means evidence is irrelevant. 3. Always consider the Prior (the base rate) before jumping to conclusions.
section_7.example: Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat' after combining his twitching ears with the base rate of cats in the neighborhood.

Only 1% of chips are actually defective.
The robot is 99% accurate but has false alarms.
If it beeps, is the chip definitely broken?
Surprisingly, most beeps come from healthy chips!

Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

            [
                "A robot scans chips for rare defects.",
                "Only 1% of chips are actually defective.",
                "The robot is 99% accurate but has false alarms.",
                "If it beeps, is the chip definitely broken?",
                "Surprisingly, most beeps come from healthy chips!"
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        line_colors = [WHITE, "#FFFF00", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF", "#FF0000"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.place_at_grid(def_text, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(hlth_text, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(line_l), Create(line_r))
        self.play(FadeIn(def_text), FadeIn(hlth_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(line_colors[2]))
        
        # From Defective: 99% accurate -> 9.9 Beep

        no_beep_def = Text("0.1 No Beep", font_size=18, color=GRAY)
        
        # From Healthy: 5% false alarm -> 49.5 Beep

        self.place_at_grid(beep_def, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(no_beep_def, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(beep_hlth, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(no_beep_hlth, "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        l1 = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["C1"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        l2 = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["C2"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        l3 = Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["C4"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        l4 = Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["C6"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        
        self.play(Create(l1), Create(l2), Create(l3), Create(l4))
        self.play(FadeIn(beep_def), FadeIn(no_beep_def), FadeIn(beep_hlth), FadeIn(no_beep_hlth))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(line_colors[3]))
        
        # Highlight 'Beep' nodes
        circle1 = Circle(color="#FF0000", radius=0.4).move_to(self.grid["C1"])
        circle2 = Circle(color="#FF0000", radius=0.4).move_to(self.grid["C4"])
        
        self.play(Create(circle1), Create(circle2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(line_colors[4]))
        
        # Calculation: P(Def|Beep)
        calc_formula = MathTex(
            "P(\\text{Defective} | \\text{Beep}) = \\frac{9.9}{9.9 + 49.5} \\approx 16.7\%",
            color="#FF0000", font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(calc_formula, "E1", "F6")
        
        # Surprising comparison
        comparison_text = Text("49.5 > 9.9 !", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(comparison_text, "D4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(calc_formula))
        self.play(FadeIn(comparison_text))

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        color_posterior = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        color_likelihood = "#00FF00" # Green
        color_prior = "#FFFF00"      # Yellow
        color_evidence = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        color_highlight = WHITE

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Independence in Bayes' Context",
            [
                "What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?",
                "The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.",
                "Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)
        # Using MathTex with parts for coloring and animation
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}",
            font_size=42
        )
        # Set colors
        formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        # index 2 is P(B|A)
        formula[2].set_color(color_likelihood)
        # index 4 is P(A)
        formula[4].set_color(color_prior)
        # index 6 is P(B)
        formula[6].set_color(color_evidence)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Replace P(B|A) with P(B)
        # New likelihood term
        new_likelihood = MathTex("P(B)", font_size=42, color=color_evidence)
        new_likelihood.move_to(formula[2].get_center())
        
        # Sliding animation: show the swap
        self.play(
            formula[2].animate.shift(UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * 0.5).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(new_likelihood, shift=DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Strike through P(B) in numerator and denominator
        strike_num = Line(
            new_likelihood.get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            new_likelihood.get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=2
        )
        strike_den = Line(
            formula[6].get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            formula[6].get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(strike_num), Create(strike_den))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final result: P(A|B) = P(A)
        final_formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "P(A)",
            font_size=42
        )
        final_formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        final_formula[2].set_color(color_prior)
        self.place_in_area(final_formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(VGroup(new_likelihood, strike_num, formula[6], strike_den, formula[3], formula[5])),
            Transform(formula[0], final_formula[0]),
            Transform(formula[1], final_formula[1]),
            Transform(formula[4], final_formula[2])
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Summary & Key Takeaways"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Bayes' Theorem is a tool for updating beliefs.",
            "- Always consider the prior base rate first.",
            "- Evidence is only useful if it's dependent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors (consistent with previous sections)
        PRIOR_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        POSTERIOR_COLOR = "#FF00FF"
        EVIDENCE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#00FF00" # Likelihood/Success

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Bayes' Theorem is a tool for updating beliefs."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        prior_text = Text("Prior", color=PRIOR_COLOR)
        posterior_text = Text("Posterior", color=POSTERIOR_COLOR)
        
        # Applying B040: Symmetrical positioning relative to center line (between 3 and 4)
        # B2 and B5 are symmetrical (Col 2 and 5)
        self.place_at_grid(prior_text, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(posterior_text, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=prior_text.get_right(), 
            end=posterior_text.get_left(), 
            color=WHITE, 
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(prior_text),
            FadeIn(posterior_text),
            Create(arrow)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Always consider the prior base rate first."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        prior_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(prior_text, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(prior_highlight))
        self.play(Indicate(prior_text, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Evidence is only useful if it's dependent."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Applying B001 and B040: Centered text using area
        evidence_text = Text("Evidence", color=EVIDENCE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(evidence_text, "D3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        cross_mark = Cross(evidence_text, stroke_color=RED)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(evidence_text))
        self.play(Create(cross_mark))
        self.wait(1)

        # Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat'
        # Clear specific visuals to make room for final demonstration
        self.play(
            FadeOut(prior_text), FadeOut(posterior_text), FadeOut(arrow),
            FadeOut(prior_highlight), FadeOut(evidence_text), FadeOut(cross_mark)
        )
        
        # Represent Sherlock Bones (Dog) and the Cat

        dog_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Text("Dog", font_size=16)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        cat_icon = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=0.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Text("Cat", font_size=16)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(dog_icon, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(cat_icon, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Sherlock Bones finding the cat
        self.play(FadeIn(dog_icon), FadeIn(cat_icon))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move dog to cat (finding it)
        # Applying B009: Path is clear
        self.play(
            dog_icon.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.play(
            dog_icon.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"] + LEFT*0.6),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Success celebration
        # Applying B023: use 'n' for Star
        success_star = Star(n=5, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.5)
        # Position star above the discovery
        success_star.move_to(self.grid["E5"] + UP*0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(success_star),
            dog_icon[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(
            success_star.animate.scale(1.5).rotate(PI/4),
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma
outline.content: Introduce the concept of 'updating belief' through a story. A detective dog named 'Sherlock Bones' hears a rustle in the bushes. He thinks there's a 10% chance it's a cat. If it were a cat, his ears would twitch with 90% certainty. His ears just twitched. Does this mean it's definitely a cat? This sets the stage for prior vs. posterior probability.
outline.example: Visual: Sherlock Bones with a thought bubble showing a 'Cat' (10%) and 'Wind' (90%). An animation shows his ears twitching as the 'new evidence'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Hook: The Detective Dog's Dilemma"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Sherlock Bones, our probabilistic detective dog.",
            "He hears a rustle in the bushes nearby.",
            "Sherlock believes there's a 10% chance it's a cat.",
            "If it's a cat, his ears twitch 90% often.",
            "His ears just twitched! Is it really a cat?"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PRIOR = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_DOG = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_CAT = "#FF69B4"
        COLOR_WIND = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Meet Sherlock Bones (Dog Icon)
        head = Circle(radius=0.5, color=COLOR_DOG, fill_opacity=1)
        left_ear = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_DOG, fill_opacity=1).rotate(PI/6)
        right_ear = Ellipse(width=0.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_DOG, fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/6)
        left_ear.shift(LEFT*0.35 + UP*0.4)
        right_ear.shift(RIGHT*0.35 + UP*0.4)
        
        eyes = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLACK).shift(LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.1),
            Dot(color=BLACK).shift(RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.1)
        )
        nose = Triangle(color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.08).rotate(PI).shift(DOWN*0.1)
        
        dog = VGroup(head, left_ear, right_ear, eyes, nose)
        self.place_at_grid(dog, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_DOG))
        self.play(FadeIn(dog))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rustle in the bushes (visualized as a shaking bush)
        bush = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN_E, fill_opacity=1).shift(RIGHT*0.2*i)
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(bush, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(bush))
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(LEFT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(LEFT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(bush.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1), run_time=0.1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sherlock believes 10% Cat / 90% Wind (Thought Bubble)
        bubble_outline = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.3, height=1.5, width=2.5, color=WHITE)
        cat_text = Text("Cat (10%)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        wind_text = Text("Wind (90%)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        thought_content = VGroup(cat_text, wind_text).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        thought_bubble = VGroup(bubble_outline, thought_content)
        self.place_at_grid(thought_bubble, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        connector_dots = VGroup(
            Dot(radius=0.05, color=WHITE),
            Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE),
            Dot(radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        connector_dots.move_to(self.grid["C4"])

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PRIOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(connector_dots), FadeIn(thought_bubble))
        # Highlight Cat as Prior
        self.play(cat_text.animate.set_color(COLOR_PRIOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # If it's a cat, his ears twitch 90% often
        twitch_prob = Text("P(Twitch | Cat) = 90%", font_size=16, color=COLOR_CAT)
        self.place_at_grid(twitch_prob, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_CAT))
        self.play(FadeIn(twitch_prob))
        
        # Twitching animation
        self.play(
            left_ear.animate.rotate(PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            right_ear.animate.rotate(-PI/12, about_point=head.get_top()),
            run_time=0.2
        )

outline.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone
outline.content: Define Independence. If A and B are independent, knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). This means the 'proportion' of A inside B is the same as A's proportion in the whole universe.
outline.example: Visual: Two circles (A and B) that don't overlap in a way that suggests dependency. If we zoom into B, the percentage of A remains exactly the same as it was in the original square.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines from storyboard
        # Title: "Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone"
        # 1. Independence means event B provides no new information.
        # 2. Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A.
        # 3. The proportion of A remains constant across the universe.
        
        self.setup_layout("Independence: The 'No Influence' Zone", [
            "Independence means event B provides no new information.",

        ])
        
        # Colors - Hex format as requested
        COLOR_A = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_B = "#00FF00"  # Green

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Independence means event B provides no new information."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Universe Square

        universe = Square(side_length=3.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(universe, "B3", "E5")
        
        u_label = Text("Universe", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(u_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Two independent circles A and B
        circle_a = Circle(radius=0.8, color=COLOR_A, fill_opacity=0.2)
        circle_b = Circle(radius=0.8, color=COLOR_B, fill_opacity=0.2)
        
        # Centers within the square
        self.place_at_grid(circle_a, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(circle_b, "D4") # Vertical overlap
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_A)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_B)
        
        # External labels to avoid bounding box overlap (B001)
        # Using Col 2 and Col 6 which are outside the B3-E5 universe box.
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(universe), FadeIn(u_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(circle_a, label_a), FadeIn(circle_b, label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Knowing B happened doesn't change the probability of A."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Highlight knowing B (the condition)
        self.play(circle_b.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.5))
        
        # Highlight intersection A in B
        # Use Intersection mobject (Community Edition v0.19.0)
        intersect = Intersection(circle_a, circle_b, color=COLOR_INTERSECT, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(intersect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The proportion of A remains constant across the universe."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERSECT))
        
        # Proportion text at top (Area A4 to A6)
        ratio_text = MathTex(
            "\\frac{P(A \\cap B)}{P(B)} = P(A)",
            font_size=32, color=COLOR_INTERSECT
        )
        self.place_in_area(ratio_text, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Definitive equality at bottom (Area F3 to F6)
        formula = MathTex("P(A|B) = P(A)", color=COLOR_INTERSECT)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "F3", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ratio_text))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(3)

outline.content: Summarize: 1. Bayes' Theorem is a way to update beliefs. 2. Independence means evidence is irrelevant. 3. Always consider the Prior (the base rate) before jumping to conclusions.
outline.example: Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat' after combining his twitching ears with the base rate of cats in the neighborhood.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Summary & Key Takeaways"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Bayes' Theorem is a tool for updating beliefs.",
            "- Always consider the prior base rate first.",
            "- Evidence is only useful if it's dependent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors (consistent with previous sections)
        PRIOR_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        POSTERIOR_COLOR = "#FF00FF"
        EVIDENCE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#00FF00" # Likelihood/Success

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Bayes' Theorem is a tool for updating beliefs."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        prior_text = Text("Prior", color=PRIOR_COLOR)
        posterior_text = Text("Posterior", color=POSTERIOR_COLOR)
        
        # Applying B040: Symmetrical positioning relative to center line (between 3 and 4)
        # B2 and B5 are symmetrical (Col 2 and 5)
        self.place_at_grid(prior_text, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(posterior_text, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=prior_text.get_right(), 
            end=posterior_text.get_left(), 
            color=WHITE, 
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(prior_text),
            FadeIn(posterior_text),
            Create(arrow)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Always consider the prior base rate first."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        prior_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(prior_text, color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(prior_highlight))
        self.play(Indicate(prior_text, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Evidence is only useful if it's dependent."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Applying B001 and B040: Centered text using area
        evidence_text = Text("Evidence", color=EVIDENCE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(evidence_text, "D3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        cross_mark = Cross(evidence_text, stroke_color=RED)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(evidence_text))
        self.play(Create(cross_mark))
        self.wait(1)

        # Final Animation: Sherlock Bones successfully identifies the 'Cat'
        # Clear specific visuals to make room for final demonstration
        self.play(
            FadeOut(prior_text), FadeOut(posterior_text), FadeOut(arrow),
            FadeOut(prior_highlight), FadeOut(evidence_text), FadeOut(cross_mark)
        )
        
        # Represent Sherlock Bones (Dog) and the Cat
        # Symmetrical positioning (B040)
        dog_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Text("Dog", font_size=16)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        cat_icon = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=0.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.3),
            Text("Cat", font_size=16)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(dog_icon, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(cat_icon, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Sherlock Bones finding the cat
        self.play(FadeIn(dog_icon), FadeIn(cat_icon))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move dog to cat (finding it)
        # Applying B009: Path is clear
        self.play(
            dog_icon.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.play(
            dog_icon.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"] + LEFT*0.6),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Success celebration
        # Applying B023: use 'n' for Star
        success_star = Star(n=5, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.5)
        # Position star above the discovery
        success_star.move_to(self.grid["E5"] + UP*0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(success_star),
            dog_icon[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(
            success_star.animate.scale(1.5).rotate(PI/4),
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
outline.content: Derive Bayes' Theorem by combining the conditional probability formulas. Show how P(A|B) allows us to reverse the condition to find P(B|A). Focus on the components: Prior P(A), Likelihood P(B|A), and Evidence P(B).

storyboard.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.
Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.
Multiply by the likelihood of seeing this evidence.
Divide by the total probability of that evidence.
Now you have the updated posterior probability.

Highlight P(B) in #00FFFF and label it 'Evidence'.
Highlight P(A|B) in #FF00FF and label it 'Posterior'.

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "The Core: Bayes' Theorem Formula"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem lets us reverse conditional probabilities.",
            "Start with your prior belief in the hypothesis.",
            "Multiply by the likelihood of seeing this evidence.",
            "Divide by the total probability of that evidence.",
            "Now you have the updated posterior probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors defined in requirements

        # Formula parts: 0:P(A|B), 1:=, 2:{, 3:P(B|A), 4:P(A), 5:\over, 6:P(B), 7:}
        # Using string splitting to allow individual coloring
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{", "P(B|A)", "P(A)", "\\over", "P(B)", "}"
        )

        self.play(

        )
        self.play(

outline.title: Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test
outline.content: Apply the theorem to a classic false-positive scenario. A 'Quality Control Robot' scans chips. 1% of chips are defective (Prior). The robot is 99% accurate but has a 5% false alarm rate. If the robot beeps, what is the actual chance the chip is broken? This highlights how even 'good' evidence can be misleading if the prior is low.
outline.example: Tree Diagram: Start with 1,000 chips. Branch into 10 Defective and 990 Healthy. Show the robot's 'Beep' paths. Most beeps actually come from healthy chips (False Positives), surprising the learner.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: The 'Broken Robot' Test",
            [
                "A robot scans chips for rare defects.",
                "Only 1% of chips are actually defective.",
                "The robot is 99% accurate but has false alarms.",
                "If it beeps, is the chip definitely broken?",
                "Surprisingly, most beeps come from healthy chips!"
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        line_colors = [WHITE, "#FFFF00", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF", "#FF0000"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(line_colors[0]))
        
        root_text = Text("1,000 Chips", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(root_text, "A3", "A4")
        self.play(Write(root_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(line_colors[1]))
        
        def_text = Text("10 Defective (1%)", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        hlth_text = Text("990 Healthy (99%)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(def_text, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(hlth_text, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        line_l = Line(self.grid["A3"], self.grid["B1"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY)
        line_r = Line(self.grid["A4"], self.grid["B5"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY)
        
        self.play(Create(line_l), Create(line_r))
        self.play(FadeIn(def_text), FadeIn(hlth_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(line_colors[2]))
        
        # From Defective: 99% accurate -> 9.9 Beep
        beep_def = Text("9.9 Beep", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        no_beep_def = Text("0.1 No Beep", font_size=18, color=GRAY)
        
        # From Healthy: 5% false alarm -> 49.5 Beep
        beep_hlth = Text("49.5 Beep", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        no_beep_hlth = Text("940.5 No Beep", font_size=18, color=GRAY)
        
        self.place_at_grid(beep_def, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(no_beep_def, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(beep_hlth, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(no_beep_hlth, "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        l1 = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["C1"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        l2 = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["C2"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        l3 = Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["C4"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        l4 = Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["C6"], buff=0.2, color=GRAY_A)
        
        self.play(Create(l1), Create(l2), Create(l3), Create(l4))
        self.play(FadeIn(beep_def), FadeIn(no_beep_def), FadeIn(beep_hlth), FadeIn(no_beep_hlth))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(line_colors[3]))
        
        # Highlight 'Beep' nodes
        circle1 = Circle(color="#FF0000", radius=0.4).move_to(self.grid["C1"])
        circle2 = Circle(color="#FF0000", radius=0.4).move_to(self.grid["C4"])
        
        self.play(Create(circle1), Create(circle2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(line_colors[4]))
        
        # Calculation: P(Def|Beep)
        calc_formula = MathTex(
            "P(\\text{Defective} | \\text{Beep}) = \\frac{9.9}{9.9 + 49.5} \\approx 16.7\%",
            color="#FF0000", font_size=32
        )
        self.place_in_area(calc_formula, "E1", "F6")
        
        # Surprising comparison
        comparison_text = Text("49.5 > 9.9 !", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(comparison_text, "D4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(calc_formula))
        self.play(FadeIn(comparison_text))
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
outline.content: Briefly explain what happens to Bayes' Theorem if events are independent. If A and B are independent, P(A|B) simply equals P(A). The evidence B becomes 'noise' and doesn't update our belief about A at all.
outline.example: Visual: A 'Bayes Machine' where the input 'Evidence B' passes through a filter. If B is independent of A, the output (Posterior) is identical to the input (Prior).

storyboard.title: Independence in Bayes' Context
lecture_lines: What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?
The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.
Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior.
animations: Show P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B).
Replace P(B|A) with P(B) using a sliding animation.
Strike through P(B) in both parts to reveal P(A).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        color_posterior = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        color_likelihood = "#00FF00" # Green
        color_prior = "#FFFF00"      # Yellow
        color_evidence = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        color_highlight = WHITE

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Independence in Bayes' Context",
            [
                "What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?",
                "The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.",
                "Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)
        # Using MathTex with parts for coloring and animation
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}",
            font_size=42
        )
        # Set colors
        formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        # index 2 is P(B|A)
        formula[2].set_color(color_likelihood)
        # index 4 is P(A)
        formula[4].set_color(color_prior)
        # index 6 is P(B)
        formula[6].set_color(color_evidence)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Replace P(B|A) with P(B)
        # New likelihood term
        new_likelihood = MathTex("P(B)", font_size=42, color=color_evidence)
        new_likelihood.move_to(formula[2].get_center())
        
        # Sliding animation: show the swap
        self.play(
            formula[2].animate.shift(UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * 0.5).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(new_likelihood, shift=DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Strike through P(B) in numerator and denominator
        strike_num = Line(
            new_likelihood.get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            new_likelihood.get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=2
        )
        strike_den = Line(
            formula[6].get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            formula[6].get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(strike_num), Create(strike_den))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final result: P(A|B) = P(A)
        final_formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "P(A)",
            font_size=42
        )
        final_formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        final_formula[2].set_color(color_prior)
        self.place_in_area(final_formula, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(VGroup(new_likelihood, strike_num, formula[6], strike_den, formula[3], formula[5])),
            Transform(formula[0], final_formula[0]),
            Transform(formula[1], final_formula[1]),
            Transform(formula[4], final_formula[2])
        )
        self.wait(2)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        color_likelihood = "#00FF00" # Green
        color_prior = "#FFFF00"      # Yellow
        color_evidence = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        color_highlight = WHITE

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Independence in Bayes' Context",
            [
                "What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?",
                "The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.",
                "Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)
        # Using MathTex with parts for coloring and animation
        # Index breakdown for MathTex("P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}"):
        # 0: P(A|B)
        # 1: =
        # 2: P(B|A)
        # 3: \cdot
        # 4: P(A)
        # 5: \over (line)
        # 6: P(B)
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}",
            font_size=42
        )
        # Set colors

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # If independent, P(B|A) = P(B)
        new_likelihood = MathTex("P(B)", font_size=42, color=color_evidence)
        new_likelihood.move_to(formula[2].get_center())
        
        # Replacement animation
        self.play(

        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Strike through P(B) in numerator and denominator

        strike_num = Line(
            new_likelihood.get_left() + LEFT*0.1,

        strike_den = Line(
            formula[6].get_left() + LEFT*0.1, 
            formula[6].get_right() + RIGHT*0.1, 
            color=RED, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(strike_num), Create(strike_den))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final result: P(A|B) = P(A)
        final_formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "P(A)",
            font_size=42
        )
        final_formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        final_formula[2].set_color(color_prior)
        
        # [Issue 45] Adjusted placement: C3 to C6, scale 1.0
        self.place_in_area(final_formula, 'C3', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(

            Transform(formula[0], final_formula[0]),
            Transform(formula[1], final_formula[1]),
            Transform(formula[4], final_formula[2])
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        color_posterior = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        color_likelihood = "#00FF00" # Green
        color_prior = "#FFFF00"      # Yellow
        color_evidence = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        color_highlight = WHITE

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Independence in Bayes' Context",
            [
                "What if evidence and hypothesis are independent?",
                "The likelihood ratio simplifies to exactly one.",
                "Our posterior belief stays identical to our prior."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B)
        # Using MathTex with parts for coloring and animation
        # Index breakdown for MathTex("P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}"):
        # 0: P(A|B)
        # 1: =
        # 2: P(B|A)
        # 3: \cdot
        # 4: P(A)
        # 5: \over (line)
        # 6: P(B)
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(A|B)", "=", "{{P(B|A)}}", "\\cdot", "{{P(A)}}", "\\over", "{{P(B)}}",
            font_size=42
        )
        # Set colors
        formula[0].set_color(color_posterior)
        formula[2].set_color(color_likelihood)
        formula[4].set_color(color_prior)
        formula[6].set_color(color_evidence)
        
        # [Issue 45] Adjusted placement: B3 to D6, scale 1.0
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B3', 'D6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # If independent, P(B|A) = P(B)
        new_likelihood = MathTex("P(B)", font_size=42, color=color_evidence)
        new_likelihood.move_to(formula[2].get_center())
        
        # Replacement animation
        self.play(
            formula[2].animate.shift(UP * 0.5).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(new_likelihood, shift=UP * 0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Strike through P(B) in numerator and denominator
        # We need to position these relative to the objects
        strike_num = Line(
            new_likelihood.get_left() + LEFT*0.1,
